summary: Incoherent 429 behavior when using multiple API keys under single tenant / unclear per-key vs per-tenant quotas
description: Customer reports receiving 429 responses on one API key while other API keys under the same tenant remain below their per-key limits. Customer expects per-key isolation for burst capacity; observed behavior suggests either a global tenant-level cap or a bug in combined token accounting for dedicated customers. Impacts production service: intermittent request failures causing degraded user workflows.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer provisions two API keys (key-A, key-B) under same tenant on Dedicated plan.
2) Send steady low-rate traffic on key-A (< configured per-key QPS).
3) Send burst traffic from multiple clients using key-B concurrently (still within per-key burst).
4) Observe 429s returned on requests signed with key-A.
5) Check console quota panels and rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-*, Retry-After).
observed_behavior: Requests authenticated with key-A receive 429s with X-RateLimit-Tenant: 0 remaining even though X-RateLimit-Key for key-A showed remaining tokens. Console shows tenant-level usage spike; per-key charts for key-A show low usage.
expected_behavior: Per-key token buckets should be independently enforced for typical burst patterns. Tenant-level quotas should only be hit when aggregate tenant usage exceeds tenant quota. Customer expects key-A to be allowed while key-B consumes bursts up to its per-key limit.
logs:
[2026-03-09T14:22:03Z] request_id=rt-9f4c tenant_id=atlas-prod api_key=key-A status=429 X-RateLimit-Key-Remaining=120 X-RateLimit-Tenant-Remaining=0 Retry-After=10
[2026-03-09T14:22:03Z] request_id=rt-9f4d tenant_id=atlas-prod api_key=key-B status=200 X-RateLimit-Key-Remaining=8 X-RateLimit-Tenant-Remaining=0
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: tenant-level burst headroom reached, causing global short-circuit to return 429s for all keys.
- Counter-evidence: per-key dashboards show key-A not near its limit.
- Checked rate-limiter shard logs: observed tenant quota sharded incorrectly when multiple keys used concurrently; one shard reported negative headroom briefly then propagated 429s.
- Reproduced in staging by simulating two API keys with dedicated pool autoscaling disabled. Observed tenant token accounting decrementing twice for some aggregated batched requests.
- Related to recent change in api-gateway: PR #3812 introduced tenant-centric fast-path optimization to short-circuit when aggregate token count low (see linked PR). Potential race when concurrent key-level checks overlap.
comments: Aisha Kapoor (CSM): Customer is observing significant user impact in their production integration; they can reproduce consistently during business hours.
Tomás Garcia (SRE): Started a targeted repro in staging; disabling gateway optimization avoided the issue in our test. Creating INT follow-up to validate fix scope (linked).

Emily Chen (Eng, Rate Limiter): Hypothesis — shard-aggregation race condition. Will add instrumentation to show per-request atomic decrements. Created PR to add a compare-and-swap guard in shard aggregator.
Customer (AtlasHealth) via email: Appreciates quick triage; requests a temporary mitigation (e.g., increase tenant headroom or enable per-key throttling override) until fix is deployed.
resolution: Workaround provided: temporarily increased tenant burst headroom for AtlasHealth and disabled the gateway fast-path optimization for their dedicated cluster (coordination with infra scheduled). Engineering patch (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3827) introduced atomic aggregation and additional telemetry; patch rolled to staging 2026-03-12 and to prod canary 2026-03-13. Follow-ups: monitor for recurrence for 72 hours, add regression test simulating multi-key bursts, and document expected per-key vs tenant behavior in support KB.
